title: A novel modulator of the Axin/beta-Catenin interaction to restore EAAT2 expression in alzheimer's disease: an in-silico and in-vitro approach.
authors: Kaur, Harminder; Saikia, Biman; Choudhary, Gajendra; Prajapat, Manisha; Ghosh, Ketaki; Ghosh, Subrata; Mondal, Prasenjit; Prakash, Ajay; Medhi, Bikash
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦Axin/beta-catenin蛋白-蛋白相互作用的小分子调节剂，用于阿尔茨海默病EAAT2表达恢复，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，且方法为分子对接与MD模拟但对象完全偏离本课题。
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder marked by synaptic dysfunction and neuronal loss, with glutamate excitotoxicity playing a central role in its pathology. The astrocytic glutamate transporter EAAT2, responsible for maintaining synaptic glutamate homeostasis, is significantly downregulated in AD. Restoration of EAAT2 expression presents a promising therapeutic strategy. This study explores the potential of modulating the Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway to enhance EAAT2 levels by targeting the Axin-1/beta-catenin interaction. Through virtual screening of 120,993 compounds from the Asinex-CNS database, five lead candidates were identified based on molecular docking, MMGBSA scores, and drug-likeness parameters. Advanced in-silico analyses-including Principal Component Analysis, Dynamic Cross-Correlation Mapping, molecular dynamics simulations, and MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations-highlighted BAS 04937103 as the most promising compound for disrupting beta-catenin degradation. In vitro validation using C6 glioma cells and primary astrocytic cultures demonstrated that BAS 04937103 enhanced beta-catenin stabilization and nuclear translocation, reduced Axin-1 expression, and significantly upregulated EAAT2 levels. These molecular effects corresponded with decreased extracellular glutamate concentrations, improved glutamate uptake, and reduced oxidative stress. Collectively, these findings establish BAS 04937103 as a novel modulator of the Axin/beta-catenin interaction with therapeutic potential in mitigating glutamate-mediated neurotoxicity in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是一种进行性神经退行性疾病，以突触功能障碍和神经元丢失为特征，其中谷氨酸兴奋性毒性在其病理过程中起核心作用。星形胶质细胞谷氨酸转运体EAAT2负责维持突触谷氨酸稳态，在AD中显著下调。恢复EAAT2表达是一种有前景的治疗策略。本研究探讨了通过靶向Axin-1/β-catenin相互作用来调节Wnt/β-catenin信号通路以增强EAAT2水平的潜力。通过对Asinex-CNS数据库中120,993种化合物进行虚拟筛选，基于分子对接、MMGBSA评分和药物相似性参数，确定了五个先导候选化合物。先进的计算机模拟分析——包括主成分分析、动态交叉相关映射、分子动力学模拟和MM/PBSA结合自由能计算——突出显示BAS 04937103是破坏β-catenin降解最有前景的化合物。使用C6胶质瘤细胞和原代星形胶质细胞培养的体外验证表明，BAS 04937103增强了β-catenin的稳定性和核转位，降低了Axin-1表达，并显著上调了EAAT2水平。这些分子效应与细胞外谷氨酸浓度降低、谷氨酸摄取改善和氧化应激减少相对应。总体而言，这些发现确立了BAS 04937103作为Axin/β-catenin相互作用的新型调节剂，在缓解阿尔茨海默病中谷氨酸介导的神经毒性方面具有治疗潜力。
